finding.text: The Process page's whole content escapes its tab panel (layout 1, requirement 1). `process/page.js` `content()` runs `await fetch(...)` and only then calls `div.c(...)`, which breaks the framework's rule "No DOM after an `await`" (doc/rules.md:75, core/View/readme.md:19). So the column lands outside the panel: at 1200 it squeezes the head to about 110px ("Tas" is clipped, one tab left) and runs off the right edge ("launches the sessio", the code block is cut). At 3440 the panel is empty and the content sits at the far right, overlapping the tab bar. Fix: capture the box first, then fill it in the fetch's callback.

The review shots are of the main site, where the page doesn't exist yet: `shots/…-Task-process/1200.png` is "Page Load Error 404" and its layout.json has `errors: 404`. Every visual answer below comes from my own headless render of the worktree's four files over the main site (`%TEMP%/rv-process/b1200.png`, `b3440.png`, `400.png`). After the fix, re-run review.mjs against the worktree.

`core/Task/files.jsonl` exists, but the diff doesn't touch it, so `process/page.js` isn't listed there (requirement 3, "files.jsonl where the folder keeps one"). If a script writes that file, its next run covers this.
At 400 every step row wraps into two lines (state on the first line; session and cost on the second, `400.png`). That is acceptable, but the state then floats on the right with nothing next to it.

The shots in the task folder are of a 404: review.mjs shot monorepo.localhost, where the branch isn't merged (layout.json errors: `404 — nothing matches "/framework/core/Task/process/"` at all four widths). I judged the page from my own headless shots of the worktree server, `qf-6.localhost`, at 1200 and 400. Re-run review.mjs against the worktree before merging.

The step list wraps badly and its columns don't line up (layout 2, wrapping 1). Each row is its own flex line, so the state, session and cost columns start at a different x on every row. At 1200, step 3 wraps to three lines ("✓ / complete", "improve-plan"). At 400, every row wraps the step name, the tick and the agent name onto 2–3 lines. It needs one grid, with columns sized to their content, and at 400 the session on its own line under the name.

The h2 headings are bigger than the content they head (sizing 3). "A real run: the readmes page, through build" takes 2 lines at 1200 and 3 at 400, which is more space than the step rows below it. A shorter heading or a smaller size would fix it.
The run reads "state **stopped**" while step 7 shows "waiting", and the page doesn't say why. The data is real, so explain it in one line, e.g. "stopped by the owner before merge".
